government.note: Parliamentary republic. The Prime Minister stays in office only while the government keeps the support of a majority of the Chamber of Deputies. The President was elected by a joint session of Parliament until a 2012 constitutional amendment introduced direct two-round elections, first used in 2013. If the presidency is vacant, some of its powers pass to the Prime Minister and some to the President of the Chamber of Deputies (or of the Senate if the Chamber is dissolved). Constitutional changes need a three-fifths majority in the Chamber of Deputies.

holders.vacant_reason: Parliament had not elected a successor when Havel's term ended (the first two ballots in January 2003 failed). Under the constitution the presidential powers were divided between the Prime Minister (Vladimír Špidla) and the President of the Chamber of Deputies (Lubomír Zaorálek) until Václav Klaus took office.

system.note: Open-list PR. Since 2002 there have been 14 constituencies matching the regions. Until 2017 seats were allocated by D'Hondt, with higher thresholds for alliances (10/15/20%). After a February 2021 Constitutional Court ruling, the current rules use the Imperiali quota in the constituencies and the Hagenbach-Bischoff quota for remaining seats, with thresholds of 5% for single parties, 8% for two-party coalitions and 11% for larger coalitions. seats_2000 is the result of the June 1998 election; mid-term changes before 1 January 2000 were not checked.

system.note: 81 single-member constituencies elected by the two-round system; one third of the seats is elected every two years for six-year terms. seats_2000 is the composition after the November 1998 Senate election by nominating party. The Four-Coalition (KDU-ČSL, Freedom Union, ODA and DEU) is recorded as one bloc because the source does not split its 26 senators.
